title: Customer Collaboration Design Lab - Runbook and Facilitation Notes
body:
Purpose and scope:
This runbook is a working facilitation guide for interactive customer ‘Design Lab’ workshops aimed at scoping a production POC of Redwood Inference. The goal is to leave the customer with a clear technical plan, success criteria, and a prioritized list of blockers plus owners. This doc is intentionally lightweight and workshop-focused (not a full sales proposal).

Primary objectives (what we must achieve by EOD):
- Validate one or two concrete product scenarios (e.g., chat assistant for support, semantic search for docs) with customer stakeholders.
- Land engineering feasibility: network, data access, model variant, and SLOs.
- Produce a 6-week POC plan with milestones, acceptance tests, and resource commitments.
- Identify top 3 risks and immediate mitigations.

Pre-work for customer (send 3 days before):
- Short questionnaire (1 page): primary success metric, protected data presence, expected throughput, desired latency SLA.
- Provide sample dataset or representative queries (anonymized).
- Confirm participants and stakeholder decision authority (who signs POC completion).
- Grant demo account + read-only access to a sample dataset (if possible) or describe sanitization constraints.

Attendees and roles (recommended):
- Customer: product manager (decision owner), engineering lead, security/compliance rep, 1–2 domain SMEs.
- Redwood: solutions engineer (facilitator), applied ML engineer (model/quantization SME), infra engineer (network/ops SME), CSM (commercial/next steps).

Run of show (4 hours recommended) - high level timeline:
- 0:00–0:15 — Welcome & objectives (SE facilitator)
  - Quick intros + decision authority check.
  - Review expected outputs and timebox rules (we’ll capture open items).
- 0:15–0:45 — Customer context & top-priority scenarios (customer PM + SMEs)
  - Ask for a very short demo of current workflow or sample tickets.
- 0:45–1:15 — Technical constraints workshop (ops/security lead + breakout)
  - Data residency, PII, network architecture, internal approval timeline.
- 1:15–1:30 — Break
- 1:30–2:30 — Live design lab: three rapid experiments (rotating small groups)
  - Experiment A (prototype flow): wireframe + sample prompts + expected outputs
  - Experiment B (data integration): sample indexing/connectivity plan
  - Experiment C (SLO/cost): traffic profile & cost projection exercise
- 2:30–3:00 — Synthesis & decision matrix (prioritize experiments for POC)
- 3:00–3:30 — Draft POC plan, milestones, owners, and acceptance tests
- 3:30–3:50 — Risks, escalation triggers, and runbook for outages during POC
- 3:50–4:00 — Next steps, immediate actions, and calendar invites

Facilitation notes and tips:
- Timebox aggressively — a visible timer helps (we usually do 10/2 minute segments for brainstorms).
- Use the decision matrix template (impact x effort x privacy risk) to force prioritization.
- Capture all open questions in a centralized Google Sheet with owners and due dates; this doc should not be the single source of truth for action items.
- If the customer asks for model benchmarking, steer to a small, representative eval set and note that thorough benching is a follow-up task.
- Soft signals: if PM cannot provide decision timelines, escalate to CSM during the 1:15–1:30 slot.

Slide outline (for a short deck to run during the workshop, speaker notes in parentheses):
1) Title / Objectives (SE) — one slide with workshop objectives and outputs
2) Customer context (Customer PM) — customer-provided bullets or live demo screenshot
3) Redwood quick architecture primer (Infra) — high-level of hosted/dedicated/private options (one-liner per option)
4) Proposed scenario flows (SE) — 2–3 small diagrams (user -> Redwood API -> backend) (keep it concrete)
5) Data & privacy mapping (Security) — where data flows, retention, masking options, KMS integration
6) Rapid experiment templates (SE) — what we’ll try in the live lab + timeboxes
7) POC mechanics / timeline (CSM) — milestones, infra needs, weekly sync cadence
8) Acceptance criteria & measurement plan (Product) — example metrics and evaluation harness
9) Risks & contingency paths (Infra & SE) — top 3 risks with mitigations
10) Owners & next steps (All) — commitments and calendar invites

Live design lab experiment instructions (detailed facilitation scripts):
- Prototype flow (30m):
  1) 5m: Present a single end-to-end user story and expected output examples.
  2) 15m: SE and PM co-author 3 prompt variants + quick quality expectations table.
  3) 10m: Decide on one variant to take into POC; record example prompts and evaluation metric.
- Data integration (30m):
  1) 10m: Customer sketches current data sources and access constraints.
  2) 10m: Infra engineer maps simplest ingestion path (batch vs streaming, connectors) and lists missing credentials/approvals.
  3) 10m: Result: a one-page ingest checklist and a small spike owner.
- SLO / Cost modeling (30m):
  1) 15m: SE captures throughput and latency targets, runs quick token cost back-of-envelope.
  2) 15m: Group decides acceptable tradeoffs (quantized models, caching, burst policies).

Technical prep checklist (validate before lab):
- Demo account provisioned and credentials shared (yes/no)
- Customer sample dataset uploaded to shared drive or accessible endpoint
- Network diagram and reachable test host (for private deployments, confirm VPN/peering windows)
- Access to an internal contact for security questions during session
- Preloaded evaluation harness (small set of prompts) in a shared repo

Acceptance criteria template (examples to edit during workshop):
- Functional: 80% of a sampled set of 50 user queries meet a quality threshold (TBD)
- Performance: 95th percentile latency < 600ms for 4 concurrent users in test harness
- Reliability: 99% successful responses across 1k test queries over 24h (smoke)
- Security: Data pipeline uses approved KMS and PI-masking checksum validated

Risk register & escalation triggers (capture live):
- Risk: Customer network / firewall blocks demo endpoints. Mitigation: Bring a sandboxed, infra-hosted dataset and run all traffic via Redwood-hosted proxy. Escalation: infra lead + customer netops, SLA: 24h.
- Risk: PII in sample dataset. Mitigation: Use anonymization script; require signed DPA addendum before sensitive PII is used. Escalation: legal & security, SLA: 72h for review.
- Risk: Decision paralysis (no clear POC sign-off). Mitigation: Require a named success approver by end of workshop; CSM to follow up with contractual timeline.

Post-workshop deliverables and owner assignments (standard cadence):
- Within 48 hours: Draft 6-week POC plan (owner: CSM)
- Within 5 business days: Technical spike tickets created and prioritized (owner: infra lead + customer eng lead)
- Within 7 business days: Initial sandbox environment provisioned (owner: infra)
- Weekly: 30-minute sync, status notes and evaluation metric updates (owner: CSM)

Deliverable quality checklist for the POC proposal:
- Clear milestones (week-by-week), owners, and acceptance tests
- Cost estimate with at least two configuration options (conservative and optimized)
- Privacy/compliance checklist and required approvals
- Known open items with owners and due dates

Appendix - quick demo script (copy/paste friendly):
- Setup: use demo account redwood-demo@example.com, model: rwd-small-8bit, endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Example POST payload (short): {
  "input": "Help me summarize the following support ticket: [ticket text]",
  "max_tokens": 150
} (note: replace with customer prompt variants captured during workshop)

Notes to self (facilitator reminders):
- Keep language simple when describing hosted vs dedicated vs private. Customers glaze over keywords like "quantization" unless prompted.
- If time is short, skip the complexity of batch caching discussion — defer to a follow-up deep dive.
- After workshop, spin up a short Confluence summary and link all action items back to a single JIRA epic (preferably the one in linked_artifacts).

Open questions to capture during session (examples):
- Who signs off on data transfer agreements for sample data?
- Can we get an internal throughput estimate from the customer’s metrics team?
- Are there existing RBAC constraints that will block our test harness?

This doc is intentionally structured for reuse across mid-enterprise and growth customers; please copy the runbook into a project folder and adapt the timing and technical depth for very large or highly regulated customers. If you adapt the doc, add your name to collaborators and update last_modified.
